attributes.body_ja:
「と言（い）えば」「と言（い）うと」「と言（い）ったら」は、「(A) と聞（き）いて、連想（れんそう）するのは (B) だ」という意味（いみ）の表現（ひょうげん）です。この三（みっ）つは、どれも同（おな）じような場面（ばめん）で使（つか）われますが、ニュアンスは少（すこ）し異（こと）なります。

「と言（い）えば」- 「(A) を話題（わだい）にするなら」という仮定的（かていてき）なニュアンス。

「と言（い）うと」- 「(A) を聞（き）くと、いつも (B) が思（おも）い出（だ）される」というニュアンス。

「と言（い）ったら」- 「(A) が話題（わだい）になる場面（ばめん）では、やっぱり (B) を思（おも）い出（だ）す」のようなニュアンス。

この文法（ぶんぽう）は、名詞（めいし）のあとに使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。たいていは、ほかの人（ひと）の発言（はつげん）を聞（き）いたことで何（なに）かを思（おも）い出（だ）して、それを話題（わだい）にするときに使（つか）います。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

この表現（ひょうげん）は、前（まえ）の発言（はつげん）を受（う）けて使（つか）われます。ただし、前（まえ）の話題（わだい）をそのまま続（つづ）けるときに使（つか）うのではありません。 話題（わだい）を変（か）えるときや、新（あたら）しい情報（じょうほう）を加（くわ）えるときに使（つか）います。
attributes.body:
と言（い）えば, と言（い）うと, and と言（い）ったら are all expressions that are translated quite closely to 'speaking of (A)', or 'if it were the case that (A)'. Each of these structures has a slightly different nuance, but are largely used in the same situations.

と言（い）えば - More hypothetical, 'were it (A)'.

と言（い）うと - More concrete, 'if it's (A)'.

と言（い）ったら - More situational, 'when it's (A)'.

These constructions are most commonly used after nouns, in response to something that has already been mentioned in the conversation (usually by someone else). The thing that has already been said is quite often the 'trigger' for someone remembering something, causing them to interject with と言（い）えば.

Caution

Although these phrases are used in response to something that has already been mentioned, their purpose is to change the topic of the conversation somehow (or to add new information), rather than continuing along with the same subject.

attributes.description: What are the differences in と言えば／と言うと／と言ったら/といえば／というと／といったら
Further breakdown and additional example sentences

attributes.body: Both can be used to shift the topic, but といえば is used after a noun to bring up something related or comment on that thing, e.g. 京都といえば、有名なお寺が多いね ('Speaking of Kyoto, there many famous temples, aren't there.'). In contrast, ところで typically starts a new sentence to introduce an unrelated topic, e.g. ところで、週末の予定は？ ('By the way, what are your plans for the weekend?').

first_relatable.title: といえば
first_relatable.meaning: Speaking of, If it were the case that

attributes.body: Both といえば and は can introduce the topic of a sentence. といえば is used when referencing something previously mentioned or known, often implying that more information will follow ('speaking of…'). は is broader and can also suggest contrast, as in 'バナナは食べたけど…' ('I ate the banana, but [not the apple]'). といえば doesn't create contrast in this way.

first_relatable.title: といえば
first_relatable.meaning: Speaking of, If it were the case that

attributes.body: While both relate to things that have just been mentioned, ～と言っても softens or qualifies assumptions, while といえば introduces a related topic. For example, 旅行と言っても日帰りだった ('Even though I say vacation, it was just a day trip') vs. 夏といえば海ですね ('If we're speaking of summer, the beach comes to mind').

second_relatable.title: といえば
second_relatable.meaning: Speaking of, If it were the case that

attributes.body: These expressions are similar in that both can be used to shift the topic, but といえば is typically used following a noun to introduce something connected to that topic, while そういえば recalls something the speaker just remembered. For example, 夏といえば花火だね ('Speaking of summer, fireworks come to mind') vs. そういえば、明日は休みだった ('Oh right, we have a holiday tomorrow').

first_relatable.title: といえば
first_relatable.meaning: Speaking of, If it were the case that

second_relatable.title: そういえば
second_relatable.meaning: Speaking of which, By the way, Come to think of it

attributes.body: Both can mean 'speaking of (A)', but differ in tone and usage. といえば often refers back to something just mentioned or known to both speaker and listener, e.g. 京都といえば、お寺が有名だね ('Speaking of Kyoto, its temples are famous.') って is a casual form used in everyday conversation, often functioning like は to casually introduce a topic, e.g. この映画って最高！ ('That movie is amazing!')
